item_name: Integrated Circuits (ICs / Microchips, Microcontrollers & SMD Packages)
hazards: Lead-tin solder on pins and BGA balls (especially in older or non-RoHS chips)
Brominated flame retardants (BFRs) and antimony trioxide in epoxy molding compounds
Trace arsenic, gallium, cadmium, and beryllium oxide in semiconductor dies and packages
safe_handling: Handle loose ICs with tweezers or gloves to avoid bent-pin punctures
Store in antistatic tubes, ESD foam, or sealed rigid containers
Keep away from moisture and avoid crushing ceramic or epoxy packages
unsafe_actions: Never burn epoxy IC packages in open air to extract gold bonding wires
Never use open-air nitric/hydrochloric acid baths to dissolve chip casings
Do not discard loose chips into regular lab dustbins or sinks
what_to_do_if_damaged: If an IC package is cracked or shattered, wear gloves and a mask to avoid inhaling fine silica/epoxy dust, sweep fragments onto paper, and seal them in a labeled e-waste container.
disposal_route: Collect in segregated electronic component bins and send to a CPCB-authorized precious-metal e-waste refiner or hazardous electronic waste facility.
recoverable_materials: Gold (internal wire bonds and lead-frame plating)
environmental_impact: Acid leaching and open burning of ICs by informal recyclers emit highly toxic dioxins, furans, and acid fumes while contaminating local water bodies with heavy metals.
